newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber ends up, gains pared with Canfor news.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber ends up, gains pared with Canfor news.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended mostly higher but gains were pared after the initial surge linked to word that the Canfor Corporation was temporarily closing four sawmills for part or all of June, traders said.
Lumber closed $5.20 per thousand board feet higher to $0.20 lower with July up $3.00 at $383.50 and September unchanged at $373.00.

News that Canfor will be taking downtime at four of its British Columbia sawmills in June added to support from reports of increased demand for cash lumber at recent lower prices. However, demand lacked follow through as traders studied the reason for the Canfor closings.
"Cash has probably come up $5 or $10 but obviously they (Canfor) wouldn't be shutting down if business was great," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.
Schmaedick did note that futures look technically more bullish after filling a gap in the charts early in the day. The gap at $383 in July came from the break last week.
